findings.title: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin with credentials
findings.description: Any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the responses.
findings.remediation: Validate Origin against an allow-list; never combine reflected origins with credentials.
findings.evidence: Origin: https://vapt-evil.example -> ACAO: https://vapt-evil.example, ACAC: True

findings.title: Exposed backup file (backup.sql)
findings.description: Database dumps expose all application data.
findings.remediation: Delete backups from the web root.

findings.title: Exposed .env file
findings.description: Environment files commonly hold database passwords and API keys.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny dotfiles, and rotate any exposed secrets.

findings.title: Exposed .git repository
findings.description: Source code and history can be downloaded, often including secrets.
findings.remediation: Block access to dotfiles/.git at the web server and never deploy the repository directory.

findings.title: SQL injection (error-based)
findings.description: A single quote in the parameter triggered a database error, indicating user input is concatenated into a SQL query.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements (never string concatenation), apply least-privilege database accounts, and return generic error messages.

findings.title: Path traversal (arbitrary file read)
findings.description: A traversal sequence in the parameter returned the contents of a system file, so attackers can read files outside the intended directory.
findings.remediation: Never build file paths from user input; map IDs to files server-side, or resolve the path and verify it stays inside an allowed base directory.

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting (XSS)
findings.description: User input is reflected into the HTML response without encoding, so injected markup is parsed by the browser. Attackers can run script in a victim's session.
findings.remediation: Contextually HTML-encode all output (use the template engine's auto-escaping), validate input, and deploy a strict Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' missing HttpOnly
findings.description: JavaScript can read this cookie, so any XSS flaw can steal it.
findings.remediation: Set the HttpOnly attribute on cookies that JavaScript does not need.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.description: Visitors can browse the directory contents, exposing files not meant to be public.
findings.remediation: Disable auto-indexing (e.g. `Options -Indexes`, `autoindex off`).

findings.title: Stack trace / debug output exposed
findings.description: Verbose errors reveal file paths, frameworks and logic useful for further attacks.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode and return generic error pages; log details server-side.

findings.title: POST form without anti-CSRF token
findings.description: A state-changing form has no visible CSRF token; a malicious site may be able to submit it on behalf of a logged-in user (verify if SameSite cookies or other defences exist).
findings.remediation: Add per-session CSRF tokens (or double-submit cookies) and validate them server-side.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: No CSP is set, so the browser has no second line of defence against XSS and data injection.
findings.remediation: Add a restrictive policy, e.g. `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set; the app can be framed by any site.
findings.remediation: Send `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`.

findings.title: Open redirect
findings.description: The application redirects to an attacker-supplied URL, enabling phishing via trusted links.
findings.remediation: Only redirect to relative paths or an allow-list of hosts; reject `//` and absolute URLs.

findings.title: Cookie 'sessionid' missing SameSite
findings.description: Without SameSite the cookie is sent on cross-site requests, aiding CSRF.
findings.remediation: Set `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`).

findings.title: Sensitive HTML comment
findings.description: Developer comments mentioning credentials/TODOs are visible to all users.
findings.remediation: Strip comments from production HTML.
findings.evidence: TODO: remove admin password (admin/admin123) before release

findings.title: X-Powered-By header discloses technology
findings.description: The backing technology/version is advertised to every client.
findings.remediation: Remove the X-Powered-By header.

findings.title: Server banner discloses version
findings.description: Exact software versions help attackers match known CVEs.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericise the Server header.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Full URLs (possibly containing tokens or IDs) may leak to third parties via the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Send `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` or stricter.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and treat uploads/text as executable content.
findings.remediation: Send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response.

findings.title: Risky HTTP methods enabled
findings.description: The server advertises DELETE, PUT, TRACE on the site root. TRACE can aid cross-site tracing; PUT/DELETE may allow unintended modification if not access-controlled.
findings.remediation: Disable methods the application does not use at the web server / framework level.
findings.evidence: Allow: DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, TRACE

findings.title: Password submitted over HTTP
findings.description: Credentials are sent unencrypted and can be sniffed on the network.
findings.remediation: Serve the whole site over HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
findings.description: Powerful browser features (camera, geolocation, ...) are not explicitly restricted.
findings.remediation: Send a `Permissions-Policy` header disabling features the app does not use.

findings.title: robots.txt lists hidden paths
findings.description: Disallowed paths are a roadmap of sensitive areas for an attacker; robots.txt is not access control.
findings.remediation: Protect sensitive paths with authentication, not obscurity.

findings.title: Site not served over HTTPS
findings.description: Traffic is unencrypted and can be read or modified in transit.
findings.remediation: Enable HTTPS (e.g. Let's Encrypt) and redirect all HTTP traffic.
